statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6471 (PostgreSQL logical decoding can dlopen arbitrary file) in 16.15 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6471/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.15 are affected), and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/4e1252ee56c33b8a1144b25b5803f47276662519 on the REL_16_STABLE branch, which adds the output_plugin_libraries setting (src/backend/replication/logical/logical.c and src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c) so that logical decoding loads only the output plugins it lists, with a default of 'pgoutput, test_decoding'; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-6471 and is in the REL_16_15 release tag and not in REL_16_14. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the code this fix changes (one of them edits the sample configuration file, postgresql.conf.sample, for a different setting, unix_socket_directories). It lists CVE-2026-6471 under its 16.15-r0 secfixes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-28, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.13 and 16.14 and are affected, while 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix. As a check, the server binary contains the setting name output_plugin_libraries and its default value 'pgoutput, test_decoding' in 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 on both architectures, and the same file in 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 does not. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
